admission.justification: The workspace focus path and mounted narrow/wide selection cases carry the panel-local focus boundary in distinct source files. Keeping page scrolling separate from tree-row reveal prevents a selected row from moving the containing review page unexpectedly. Earlier OR-R033 geometry and origin evidence remain historical, not a fresh result.

applicability: Answered in-tree selections of the mounted intent reviewer while their focus request remains eligible.
conditions: The caller requests keepTree for a compact family/member row, traversal control or main-page member selection.
The answered-selection focus path uses preventScroll and revealTreeRow; that helper adjusts only the nearest tree panel after measuring its visible bounds and overlaid controls.
The moved-focus guard runs before landing the selection. Failed/refused reads retain the distinct stacked status-reveal path of INV-BMFR2T.
exclusions: No retained promise to scroll the reading-area start on an answered stacked selection; that earlier guarantee is superseded by panel-local row reveal.
No new browser geometry or runtime acceptance is inferred from the mounted source assertions.
Refresh scroll-only requests and lane/file destinations keep their separate owners.

evidence: browser/final-vs-pre.json (36 of 36 answered in-tree activations at 390 revealed; 62 of 62 steps at 1600 unchanged); mutations D1-a to D1-f

statement: An eligible answered in-tree selection focuses its selected row without native scrolling and reveals that row through the tree panel’s local scroll owner at either layout width. Outside selections retain their native-focus path.
